claims.text: What the strip looks like Some types have typical patterns: LQTS1 wide T waves; LQTS2 low-voltage, notched T waves; LQTS3 a long ST segment with normal-looking T waves.
claims.quote: Some forms of LQTS are also associated with particular ECG patterns: LQTS1: Wide T waves LQTS2: Low voltage, notched T-waves LQTS3: Long-ST segment with normal appearing T-waves
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) QTc (adults): normal < 0.43 s (men) and < 0.45 s (women); prolonged when > 0.44 to 0.45 s (men) or > 0.46 to 0.47 s (women)
claims.quote: In adults, normal QTc values are < 0.43 second for males and < 0.45 second for females and are considered prolonged when > 0.44 to 0.45 second for males or > 0.46 to 0.47 second for females
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: A normal QTc doesn't exclude it: found in 25 to 50% of gene-positive cases; at the moment of torsades, though, the QTc is essentially always prolonged
claims.quote: Given the multiplicity of factors affecting the QTc, a normal QTc, found in 25 to 50% of gene mutation-positive LQTS cases, does not exclude the diagnosis (3, 4, 5). Nevertheless, at the moment of torsade de pointes VT, the QTc is essentially always prolonged.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Pattern caution: neither triggers nor ECG findings are very specific, so don't use them to confirm the type or direct genetic testing
claims.quote: Neither arrhythmia triggers nor ECG findings are very specific and should not be used to confirm the type or to direct genetic testing.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Diagnosis established: resting QTc ≥ 0.46 s with documented torsades, or syncope/cardiac arrest with stress, when no other cause of a long QT is present
claims.quote: When a patient has a resting QTc interval ≥ 0.46 second and documented torsade de pointes VT or syncope/cardiac arrest with stress in the absence of other causes of a prolonged QT interval, the diagnosis of a congenital long QT interval syndrome is established (6).
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Modified Schwartz score, ECG points (table): QTc ≥ 480 ms 3; QTc 460–479 ms 2; QTc 450–459 ms (males only) 1; QTc ≥ 480 ms in the 4th minute of exercise recovery 1; torsades 2; T-wave alternans 1; notched T wave in 3 leads 1; resting heart rate < 2nd percentile for age 0.5
claims.quote: QTc ≥ 480 msec | 3‡ | QTc 460-479 msec | 2 | QTc 450-459 msec (males only) | 1 | QTc ≥ 480 msec during 4th minute of recovery from an exercise test | 1 | Torsades de pointes arrhythmia§ | 2 | T wave alternans | 1 | Notched T wave in 3 leads | 1 | Resting heart rate < 2nd percentile for age | 0.5
claims.locator: Modified Schwartz Score for Long QT Syndrome (LQTS)

claims.text: Score: ≤ 1 low, 1.5–3 intermediate, ≥ 3.5 high probability
claims.quote: SCORE: ≤ 1 low probability; 1.5–3 intermediate probability; ≥ 3.5 high probability
claims.locator: Modified Schwartz Score for Long QT Syndrome (LQTS)

claims.text: Modified diagnostic score: ≥ 3.0 is diagnostic of LQTS; QTc ≥ 480 ms scores 3.5; congenital deafness is removed; a pathogenic mutation scores 3.5
claims.quote: In the modified long QT syndrome diagnostic score: A score ≥ 3.0 is diagnostic of LQTS Congenital deafness is removed as a criterion The score for a QTc ≥ 480 msec is 3.5 A pathogenic mutation is added as a criterion, earning 3.5 points
claims.locator: Modified Schwartz Score for Long QT Syndrome (LQTS)

claims.text: May present first as: fetal or neonatal bradycardia, or 2:1 AV block
claims.quote: Fetal or neonatal bradycardia or 2:1 atrioventricular block may also be the initial presentation of a congenital long QT syndrome.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Borderline QT or genotype-positive with a normal resting QT: exercise testing, because some abnormalities appear only during or after exercise
claims.quote: Patients with borderline QT intervals suspected of having LQTS, or those with a LQTS genotype but a normal resting QT interval, should have exercise testing, because some abnormalities appear only during or after exercise (5, 7).
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: genetic disorders of cardiac ion channel function or regulation (channelopathies) that prolong the ventricular myocyte action potential, seen as a prolonged QTc
claims.quote: The congenital long QT interval syndromes result from genetic disorders of cardiac ion channel function or regulation (channelopathies) that prolong ventricular myocyte action potential duration as reflected by prolongation of the rate-corrected QT interval on the ECG
claims.locator: Pathophysiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: The dysfunction may be loss of function of repolarizing potassium channels, or gain of function of depolarizing sodium or calcium channels
claims.quote: The dysfunction may involve: Loss of function of repolarizing potassium current channels OR Gain of function of depolarizing sodium or depolarizing calcium current channels
claims.locator: Pathophysiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Why torsades: the long action potential favors early afterdepolarizations, which can reactivate neighboring repolarized myocytes; risk depends on how long the QTc is, particularly > 0.50 s
claims.quote: Prolongation of action potentials increases the probability of transmembrane voltage oscillations occurring during the depolarized myocyte action potential (early afterdepolarizations). If the action potential durations of myocytes in a local area vary, these oscillations may reactivate neighboring myocytes that have repolarized and thus create torsades de pointes ventricular tachycardia (TdP VT). The risk of TdP VT is dependent on the degree of QTc prolongation, particularly if it is > 0.50 second (1, 2).
claims.locator: Pathophysiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Types: more than 15 described; the vast majority are LQTS1, LQTS2 or LQTS3, all autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance
claims.quote: More than 15 forms of LQTS have been described; the vast majority of cases are LQTS1, LQTS2, or LQTS3. These 3 forms are inherited as autosomal dominant disorders with incomplete penetrance
claims.locator: Etiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: LQTS1: loss of function of KCNQ1 (slow outward potassium current, IKs); 40 to 55% of gene-positive cases
claims.quote: Long QT syndrome type 1 (LQTS1): Loss-of-function mutation of gene KCNQ1, which encodes an adrenergic-sensitive Kv7.1 channel responsible for the slow outward potassium current (IKs) (40 to 55% of gene-positive cases)
claims.locator: Etiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: LQTS2: loss of function of KCNH2 (hERG channel, rapid outward potassium current, IKr); 30 to 45% of gene-positive cases
claims.quote: Long QT syndrome type 2 (LQTS2): Loss-of-function mutation of gene KCNH2, which encodes the hERG channel responsible for the rapid outward potassium current (IKr) (30 to 45% of gene-positive cases
claims.locator: Etiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: LQTS3: gain of function of SCN5A (inward sodium current, INa); 5 to 10% of gene-positive cases
claims.quote: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQTS3): Gain-of-function mutation of gene SCN5A, which encodes the Nav1.5 channel responsible for the inward sodium current (INa) (5 to 10% of gene-positive cases)
claims.locator: Etiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Rare syndromic forms: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen (congenital sensorineural deafness), Andersen-Tawil, Timothy syndrome
claims.quote: Rare forms of LQTS with additional clinical features have been described including Jervell and Lange Nielsen syndrome (with congenital sensorineural deafness), Andersen-Tawil syndrome (with period paralysis and craniofacial dysmorphisms), and Timothy syndrome
claims.locator: Etiology of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Congenital LQTS affects at least 1 in 2000 and causes about 15 to 20% of cardiac arrests left unexplained after evaluation
claims.quote: The incidence of congenital LQTS is at least 1 in 2000 (1, 2) and is the cause of approximately 15 to 20% of cardiac arrests that are unexplained after clinical evaluation
claims.locator: Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Symptoms No symptoms unless torsades occurs: palpitations, near-syncope, syncope or sudden death; some have myoclonic jerks during syncope and may be wrongly worked up for epilepsy
claims.quote: The LQTS are asymptomatic unless TdP VT occurs, which can cause palpitations, near-syncope, syncope, or sudden death. Some patients experience myoclonic jerks during syncope; they may incorrectly have a diagnosis of epilepsy pursued.
claims.locator: Symptoms and Signs of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Torsades is often self-terminating, but it may degenerate into ventricular fibrillation and cause cardiac arrest
claims.quote: TdP VT is often self-terminating. However, it may degenerate into ventricular fibrillation and cause cardiac arrest.
claims.locator: Symptoms and Signs of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Typical triggers: LQTS1 physical exertion (particularly swimming) or emotional stress; LQTS2 sudden loud noises such as an alarm clock; LQTS3 rest or sleep
claims.quote: Some forms of LQTS are more associated with certain triggers than others: LQTS1: Physical stress/exertion, particularly swimming, or emotional stress LQTS2: Sudden loud noises like an alarm clock LQTS3: Resting or sleep
claims.locator: Symptoms and Signs of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Treatment Acute torsades: defibrillation for torsade-induced VF and IV magnesium sulfate; temporary pacing may help frequent or long runs (raising the heart rate shortens the QT)
claims.quote: Details of treatment of torsade de pointes ventricular tachycardia are discussed elsewhere but include defibrillation for torsade-induced VF and magnesium sulfate IV. Patients with frequent or long runs of torsades de pointes ventricular tachycardia may benefit from treatment to shorten the QT interval by increasing the heart rate using temporary pacing.
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Unlike drug-induced torsades, acute IV therapy is a beta blocker rather than isoproterenol
claims.quote: Unlike medication-induced acquired torsade de pointes, the mainstay of acute IV pharmacotherapy is IV beta-blocker rather than IV isoproterenol.
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Long term: avoid genotype-specific triggers and QT-prolonging conditions or medications (see CredibleMeds)
claims.quote: Long-term treatment to prevent sudden death includes avoidance of genotype-specific triggers (including careful discussion of strenuous exercise in LQTS1 and LQTS2) and QTc-prolonging conditions or medications (see CredibleMeds for up-to-date information)
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Beta blocker: recommended with QTc prolongation or symptoms (most effective in LQTS1 or LQTS2); prefer a long-acting non-selective one (e.g., nadolol, slow-release propranolol)
claims.quote: Beta-blocker therapy is recommended for patients who have LQTS with QTc interval prolongation or who are symptomatic (most effective with LQTS1 or LQTS2) (1,2). Beta-blocker therapy is reasonable in asymptomatic patients with LQTS and a normal QTc interval (1, 2). When a beta-blocker is used, a long-acting, non-selective beta-blocker (eg, nadolol, slow-release propranolol) is preferred.
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: LQTS3: mexiletine is added when a beta blocker doesn't relieve symptoms
claims.quote: When beta-blocker therapy is ineffective at relieving symptoms in patients with LQTS3, mexiletine is added (2).
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: ICD: indicated after resuscitated cardiac arrest or cardiac syncope despite a beta blocker; may be considered with QTc > 500 ms on a beta blocker even when asymptomatic
claims.quote: An ICD is indicated in patients who have been resuscitated after cardiac arrest and in those who have cardiac syncope despite therapy with a beta-blocker. An ICD may also be considered for patients with a QTc > 500 msec while on a beta-blocker even when asymptomatic
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Left heart (stellate ganglion) denervation may also be used
claims.quote: Left heart (stellate ganglion) denervation may also be used (3).
claims.locator: Treatment of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Family: first-degree relatives get a clinical evaluation and ECG; genetic testing when the index case has a known mutation
claims.quote: First-degree relatives of the index case should have clinical evaluation (ie, to detect symptoms suggestive of arrhythmia) and ECG. Thereafter, the first-degree relatives of any newly identified patients undergo similar assessment (cascade screening). Genetic testing is performed when the index case has a known mutation.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes

claims.text: Your EKG notes give a normal QTc of < 440 ms for men and < 460 ms for women.
claims.quote: Normal QTc: < 440 ms (men), < 460 ms (women)

claims.quote: In adults, normal QTc values are < 0.43 second for males and < 0.45 second for females and are considered prolonged when > 0.44 to 0.45 second for males or > 0.46 to 0.47 second for females
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Long QT Interval Syndromes
